description:
The Raffelsberger Hof was built in 1574 as a shipmaster's house, according to the hotel's listings, at a time when shipping on the Danube shaped the Wachau. It is a historic town house, not a castle: a protected building in the historic centre of Weißenkirchen, a wine village in the Wachau.

Today it is a four-star bed and breakfast with air-conditioned rooms and an outdoor pool in its grounds, and its Renaissance vaults house a lounge where guests can taste local wines. It stands in the Wachau, the valley between Melk and Krems, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape of terraced vineyards along the Danube.
history: The Raffelsberger Hof was built in 1574 as the house of a Danube shipmaster in Weißenkirchen, one of the wine villages of the Wachau. The Renaissance building is protected as a monument and now operates as a bed and breakfast, with guest rooms, a lounge in its old vaults and an outdoor pool.

faqs.question: Is the Raffelsberger Hof a castle?
faqs.answer: No. It is a Renaissance shipmaster's house built in 1574 in the centre of Weißenkirchen, protected as a historic building and now run as a bed and breakfast.

faqs.question: Does the Raffelsberger Hof have a restaurant?
faqs.answer: It is a bed and breakfast with breakfast included; there is a wine lounge in the vaults, but no restaurant for dinner.

hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are in the Renaissance house in the village centre; ask the hotel which floor your room is on
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The house stands at Weißenkirchen 54 in the centre of Weißenkirchen in der Wachau, on the Danube in Lower Austria, with train access according to Booking. Booking lists free private parking with electric charging.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €208/night for a Small Double Room on a high floor with a double bed, air conditioning, a private bathroom, a flat-screen TV and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast and free cancellation included on the rate seen (no prepayment); a 22 m² Double Room was around €242, a Superior Double Room around €252 and a Suite around €292. Booking shows a small tax charge (about €5) separately.

**On-site:** An outdoor pool, a wine lounge in the Renaissance vaults, free parking and free Wi-Fi. It is a bed and breakfast, so there is no restaurant for dinner.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one mid-April 2027 night, so check your own dates on Booking; Booking showed no availability for late January. The building is a Renaissance town house rather than a castle.

**Combine with:** [Dürnstein Castle](/castles/austria/durnstein-castle), the ruin where Richard the Lionheart was held, and [Dürnstein Palace](/castles/austria/durnstein-palace), both about 4 km downstream in Dürnstein, and [Aggstein Castle](/castles/austria/aggstein-castle), about 10 km further up the Danube.
